newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Christmas wind-down sees Singapore stocks weaker.
newsitem.headline: Christmas wind-down sees Singapore stocks weaker.

text.p: The Christmas wind-down was expected to leave Singapore stocks slightly weaker on Tuesday, dealers said.
With little activity in the market, open only for the morning session and closing for the day at 0430 GMT, dealers said they were marking time until lunch.
"We're just counting the minutes here," one institutional dealer said. "There'll be no Christmas crackers in the market today."
This was reflected in early trade as the key Straits Times Industrials Index sliped 2.77 points to 2,193.09 at 0230 GMT.
Among 48 losers and 71 gainers in the first 90 minutes of trade there were few highly active shares.
The biggest volume deal of the early session was a 5.5 million off-market trade of shares in Kuala Lumpur Industries, an over-the-counter stock.
Total market volume stood at 21.0 million units at 0230 GMT.

Early gainers included property firm City Developments and drinks company Fraser & Neave, both up Singapore $0.10. Early losers saw port services company China Merchants drop back Hong Kong $0.80 to HK$4.40 and Singapore Press's foreign share tranche slip S$0.20 to S$26.70.
